clue.text: Stop imitating a hen and talk turkey

definitions.meaning: read literally, cease the clucking noise a hen makes
an idiom meaning drop the chatter and get down to business

explanation.surface: A farmyard instruction to quit clucking and speak plainly, with a poultry pun on turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The literal hen-noise reading and the idiomatic 'stop chattering, get to the point' reading are the two definitions; 'and' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stop the idle chatter and talk business, exactly as talking turkey means speaking frankly.

clue.text: The person responsible for pair I introduced to sect

indicators.note: the pair and I are put into the sect

parts.note: a cult is a sect

explanation.surface: Someone responsible for bringing a couple into a cult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced to' is the container signal: the pair and I go into the sect, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: The one who did the wrong deed is the guilty party, the person responsible.

clue.text: Ready muscle accompanying this gangster

parts.note: thew is an old word for muscle or sinew
herewith means along with this, enclosed
Al Capone was the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: A muscular henchman is ready to accompany the gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is not willing but money: the readies are cash, as is this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money, the readies, means available cash, the means needed to do something.

clue.text: Reduced visibility, we hear, in part of London

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for reduced visibility is said out loud

parts.note: haze is mist that reduces visibility

explanation.surface: Poor visibility is reported in one district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: HAYES is a district in west London, in the borough of Hillingdon; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a district of west London, so an example of a part of the city.

clue.text: He's liable to crow, crafty inventor, in speech

indicators.note: in speech signals that the inventor's name is to be said out loud

parts.note: Sir Christopher Cockerell invented the hovercraft, a craft

explanation.surface: A sly inventor is prone to boasting when making a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crafty' is not sly: Cockerell's invention was the hovercraft, a craft; 'crow' means a rooster's call, not boasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A young male fowl is the bird that crows at dawn, described here by its call.

clue.text: Arrive shortly at old lake resort

indicators.note: shortly means the word for arrive is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: Arriving soon at a historic lakeside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops the final E of COME; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Italian town on its lake of the same name, a well-known holiday resort.

clue.text: With sticky fingers, cleans our act up

indicators.note: to act up is to misbehave, so the letters of cleans our are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Thieves with sticky fingers clean up their act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'act up' (misbehave) signals the anagram of CLEANS OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sticky-fingered is a slang way to describe being given to theft, i.e. thieving.

clue.text: Lavishly celebrate launch

definitions.meaning: to spend freely and celebrate in style
read literally, to shove a vessel off into the water

explanation.surface: A ship launch is celebrated extravagantly.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for splashing out is also, read literally, launching a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to spend generously on a celebration; read literally it means set a vessel afloat.

clue.text: Having a doctor with oxygen — it is handy

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
taken as written

explanation.surface: Having a doctor on hand along with oxygen is useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having', 'with' and 'is' are link words between the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being skilful and dexterous with the hands is a synonym of being handy.

clue.text: Wary, lascivious look at beauty's derriere

parts.note: a leer is a lustful, sly glance

indicators.note: the backside, so the last letter of the word beauty's

explanation.surface: Someone is suspicious of a lecherous ogler eyeing a beauty's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derriere' (bottom) takes the final letter of 'beauty's'; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being suspicious and cautious of something is a direct synonym of being wary.

clue.text: Be persuaded to visit

definitions.meaning: to change one's mind and agree after argument
to drop in at someone's home

explanation.surface: Someone is talked into calling on a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of the phrasal verb: to be won over, and to call at someone's house; 'to' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both yield to persuasion and pay a casual call on someone at home.

clue.text: Given makeover, has chap dressed in russet?

indicators.note: the chap and has are clothed in the colour, so they go inside it

parts.note: russet is a reddish-brown, taken as red
taken as written
a chap is a man, he

explanation.surface: A man gets a makeover and is now dressed in reddish-brown clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed in' is the container signal, picturing the chap clothed in a russet colour; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reworked and presented again in new form has been given a makeover, a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Music produced by number attending college

indicators.note: attending means going along with, so the number sits beside the college

parts.note: tech is short for a technical college

explanation.surface: A piece of music is performed by a student number at a college concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attending' signals the two pieces sit side by side; 'produced by' is a link. A tech is a British technical college.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a genre of electronic dance music, so it is an example of music.

clue.text: Look likely to cover low card finally with a higher one

indicators.note: a card game image: the low card's end is covered by laying another card over it
points the replacement at the last letter of the low card

parts.note: a three is a low playing card
a ten is a higher card than a three

explanation.surface: A card player seems about to cover a low card with a higher one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' and 'finally' replace the final E of THREE with A TEN, giving THRE + ATEN.
explanation.definitionFit: When clouds or trouble seem imminent they threaten, i.e. appear likely to happen.

clue.text: Very high voice one young lady piped up in

indicators.note: in places the one and the young lady inside the voice

parts.note: alto is a singing voice
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word for young lady is read backwards

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried lady

explanation.surface: A young lady pipes up in a very high singing voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piped up' reverses the young lady and 'in' is the container signal. 'Very high voice' looks like the definition, but 'voice' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This musical term means in the highest register, very high in pitch.

clue.text: Does it make any difference to Shaw? Yes, it does

indicators.note: the reply that it does make a difference tells us the words to and Shaw are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it matters to George Bernard Shaw, and answers that it does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes, it does' (it does make a difference) is the anagram signal on TO SHAW.
explanation.definitionFit: The dismissive retort asks whether something matters at all, the same question as does it make any difference.

clue.text: Climbing tree, a monster chestnut, in stone circle

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going up, so the tree and the monster are read backwards together

parts.note: the elm is a tree
an orc is a monster of fantasy
ch is the abbreviation for chestnut, as a horse colour

explanation.surface: A monstrous tree climber clambers up a chestnut near some standing stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' reverses ELM + ORC together, giving CROMLE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This prehistoric structure of standing stones is a dolmen, sometimes used for a stone circle.

clue.text: It's extremely rainy round this part of South Africa

parts.note: so means very or extremely
rainy weather is wet
the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain region of South Africa has a very wet climate.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces run in order; 'It's' and 'this' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the famous township in Johannesburg, so an example of a place in South Africa.

clue.text: Smart tart

definitions.meaning: stylish and smart, as in a well-dressed person
sharp or curt in manner, as in a tart reply

explanation.surface: A pithy description of a well-dressed woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Two adjective senses: stylish, and brusque or sharp-tongued.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both stylish (a sharp dresser) and curt (a short, tart reply).

clue.text: Peevish greeting can precipitate a quarrel

parts.note: peevish means irritable, cross
a bow is a greeting with the head or body

explanation.surface: An irritable hello may start an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: A quarrel is also a crossbow bolt, so the definition describes a weapon that shoots one, not a row.
explanation.definitionFit: This weapon fires short heavy bolts called quarrels, so it is a thing that can launch one.

clue.text: Fresh food items —- few this fresh

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters of few this are made afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's note that there are few fresh items today.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'fresh' is the anagram signal on FEW THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw, uncooked fish sold at the counter is described this way, so it is fresh food.

clue.text: Painter loosened in strait

indicators.note: loosened means the letters of strait are freed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter is stuck in a narrow channel and freed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosened' signals the anagram of STRAIT; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is a kind of visual creator, so this is the broader category word for one.

clue.text: Broadcast about family member, one leaving the country

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the broadcast goes round the relative

parts.note: to emit is to send out a signal, broadcast
a gran is a grandmother, a family member

explanation.surface: A broadcast story about a relative who is moving abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal: the broadcast word goes round the relative. 'Broadcast' looks like an anagram signal but is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who departs their homeland to settle abroad is exactly a person leaving the country.

clue.text: Good architect becomes champ

parts.note: John Nash was the Regency architect of Regent Street

explanation.surface: A good architect becomes a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champ' is not a champion but the verb to chew or bite noisily; 'becomes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to bite or chew noisily, close in sense to grinding the teeth together.

clue.text: Black vessel following watercourse

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A dark vessel moves along a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: BURN is a Scottish and northern English word for a stream; 'following' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stream in Scotland is called this, so it is a kind of watercourse.

clue.text: Cliché from Pinero's first play

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Pinero's

parts.note: play is freedom of movement or scope, latitude

explanation.surface: A tired phrase found in the first drama of the playwright Arthur Wing Pinero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a drama but means scope or slack, as in play in a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A trite, overused remark is a cliché, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: First class blend of oil used in mayonnaise

parts.note: A1 means first class, read as AI

indicators.note: a blend mixes things, so the letters of oil are mixed up

explanation.surface: A top-quality oil blend goes into making mayonnaise.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first class) is written AI; 'used in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This Provençal sauce is a garlic mayonnaise, so it is a kind of mayonnaise.

clue.text: Blue hair man is sporting evokes cheers

parts.note: blue means sad, down

indicators.note: sporting means wearing, so the hair wears the man inside it

parts.note: thatch is a thick head of hair
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A gloomy man with a striking hairstyle prompts a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is sporting' is the container signal: the hair wears the man. 'evokes' is a link, and 'Blue' means sad, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a drinking toast said before downing a drink, used just like cheers.
